title: Lancaster Street West high-rise rental proposal deferred
subtitle: Traffic, tenant displacement and heritage houses drove the deferral; Nelson Avenue condominium homes recommended with a taller-fence buffer and lower heights.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee spent most of its meeting on a proposal for five high-rise rental buildings at 528-550 Lancaster Street West, with about 1,300 units, plus a related rezoning at 26 Bridge Street West to receive two relocated heritage-interest houses. The committee recommended deferring the matter to the May 29, 2023 Council meeting {{vote:m1}}. Staff are to report back on transportation concerns, possible community benefit funding in place of moving the houses, and housing options for current tenants.

Many residents spoke against the project, citing traffic, parking, safety, loss of mature trees and wildlife habitat, and the displacement of tenants. Supporters pointed to the need for purpose-built rental housing. The deferral gives time for talks with the developer and for the Region of Waterloo to say more about road and active transportation plans.

The committee also recommended approving a rezoning and draft plan of vacant land condominium for 23 single detached homes at 67 and 71 Nelson Avenue {{vote:m2}}. The approval includes changes agreed with a neighbour: a taller fence, a landscaped buffer and lower building heights along the northern boundary.

decisions.item: Lancaster Street West and Bridge Street West applications
decisions.detail: The committee recommended deferring the official plan and zoning amendments for the Lancaster high-rise project and the Bridge Street rezoning to the May 29, 2023 Council meeting, so staff can report on transportation, alternative community benefit funding in place of relocating the heritage-interest houses, and housing for tenants.

The committee recommended approving the zoning amendment for 67 and 71 Nelson Avenue as amended, including an 8-foot fence, a landscaped buffer and an 8-metre height limit on lots next to northern neighbours.

decisions.item: Nelson Avenue draft plan of condominium
decisions.detail: The committee recommended draft approval of the vacant land condominium for 67 and 71 Nelson Avenue and part of the undeveloped Tagge Street right-of-way, subject to the conditions in the staff report.
The committee recommended that no further public notice be required for the revised Nelson Avenue zoning by-law under Section 34(17) of the Planning Act.

debate: Delegates opposed to the Lancaster project said traffic on Lancaster Street and Bridgeport Road is already heavily congested, and that the developer's traffic counts were taken during COVID-era reopening. They also said a parking rate of 0.6 per unit would push cars onto nearby streets.

Tenants and neighbours raised displacement. One tenant said they had received no offer or contact from the developer, while the developer said tenants were offered units next door at current rent. Staff said tenant accommodation cannot be required through planning conditions but offered to follow up with both sides.

Delegates and some councillors raised concerns about the loss of mature trees and wildlife habitat. Staff said no environmental impact study was required, and a tree preservation plan with compensation planting was done. Staff also said Indigenous consultation was not done, because criteria are still being developed.

Supporters said the project adds much-needed purpose-built rental housing in an urban corridor near transit. One speaker urged reduced parking and more bike storage. Staff said that if Council refused the applications, an appeal to the Ontario Land Tribunal was likely to succeed.

Councillors questioned the cost of moving the two houses, which would be gutted, and whether that money could instead go to community benefits such as parks or tenant support. The developer said it was open to this. At Nelson Avenue, a resident objected to the density, traffic, lighting and sale of part of Tagge Street, while the proponent's planner said the revised by-law reflected talks with a neighbour.
